Analysis: Both hypotheses propose targeting mechanotransduction pathways in TAMs to affect liver cancer progression, but Hypothesis 1 presents a more coherent and directly testable model. Its novel idea of a self‐reinforcing loop, where increased matrix stiffness drives M2 polarization and, in turn, further stiffens the matrix, is novel and plausible, although it requires deeper mechanistic detail. In contrast, Hypothesis 2, while incorporating the innovative aspect of metabolic reprogramming via the integrin‐FAK‐HIF1α axis, suffers from terminological ambiguities (notably the counterintuitive description of macrophage phenotypes) and a less clear mechanistic pathway, which could compromise both its plausibility and testability. Safety considerations appear comparable for both, though Hypothesis 1’s pathway is more directly linked to established integrin/FAK signaling. Overall, Hypothesis 1 stands out as more straightforward to experimentally validate with a clearer conceptual framework.
